policy_title: Enhance animal welfare and end harmful practices
stated: Establish a new Commission on Animal Protection to oversee rules protecting animals from cruelty, uphold their rights as sentient beings, and apply the highest standards to companion, farm, and wild animals. This includes banning all blood sports, including trail hunting and the commercial shooting of game birds, strengthening and extending the 2004 Hunting Act, introducing a licensing scheme for animal ownership, and replacing breed-specific legislation for dogs. The policy also campaigns against badger culling, funding research into cattle vaccination for Bovine TB, and investing in better farm biosecurity and badger vaccination. It pushes for an end to factory farming, enforcing maximum stocking densities, prohibiting the routine use of antibiotics in farm animals, and campaigning for a complete ban on cages, close confinement, and deliberate mutilation of farm animals.

source.quote: Elected Greens will seek to create a new Commission on Animal Protection, responsible for overseeing all rules designed to protect animals from cruelty and upholding their rights as sentient beings not to be subjected to undue suffering. This Commission will ensure that the highest standards of animal protection are applied to companion animals, farm animals and wildlife - and that these standards underpin decision making by public bodies too. Elected Greens will push for: • A ban on all blood sports, including trail hunting and strengthening and extending the 2004 Hunting Act. Elected Greens would push for ending the exploitation of animals, including horses and greyhounds in racing. Green MPs will introduce a licensing scheme for the ownership of all kept animals and replace outdated breed-specific legislation for dogs with an updated dog control law. Green MPs will campaign against badger culling. We will fund research into a sensitive test to enable cattle vaccination as part of a meaningful strategy to control the spread of the disease. We will also invest in better farm biosecurity and badger vaccination. Elected Greens will push for an end to factory farming, enforce maximum stocking densities and prohibit the routine use of antibiotics in farm animals. Greens will campaign for a complete ban on cages and close confinement, and on the deliberate mutilation of farm animals.

consolidated_from: Create a Commission on Animal Protection
Ban blood sports and strengthen animal cruelty laws
End badger culling and invest in Bovine TB research
End factory farming and improve farm animal welfare

bearing_set.reason: Banning factory farming, enforcing maximum stocking densities, and prohibiting cage systems would materially raise food production costs, with a plausible, non-negligible pass-through to food prices for households.

Prohibiting routine antibiotic use in farm animals directly targets antimicrobial resistance (AMR), a documented threat to the effectiveness of medical treatments — a genuine, non-negligible healthcare system effect.

Ending factory farming and restricting intensive livestock practices would materially reduce agricultural greenhouse-gas emissions (methane, nitrous oxide) and nitrogen-pollution of waterways — a direct, non-negligible environmental quality effect.

Introducing a licensing scheme for animal ownership and replacing breed-specific dog legislation directly targets dangerous-dog incidents on public streets, earning a real (if contested) verdict on the 'are streets safe' indicator.

Banning trail hunting, commercial game-bird shooting (currently legal activities), and introducing mandatory licensing for animal ownership all impose new state restrictions on what people may lawfully do — direct worsening of freedom-from-state-coercion and property/activity-rights indicators.

The commercial game-bird shooting sector is a significant rural enterprise (direct banning removes an established commercial activity); restructuring intensive farming affects agricultural-sector investment and business dynamism — both represent non-negligible shocks to rural economic opportunity and living standards.

membership_note: Policy has five genuine bearings: it raises food costs (O2), improves long-run healthcare via AMR reduction (O3), improves environment and biodiversity (O6), worsens personal liberty by criminalising currently lawful activities (O10), and negatively affects rural economic opportunity and investment in affected sectors (O13).
